purpose: Diagnose whether the r19 in-path answer/length divergence requires c32 inter-sample contention; not a population quality or adoption test.
selection: Post-hoc r19 anchors fixed before r20 execution: one 3/3 cap-associated loss, one non-cap paired loss, and the nearest-length stable both-correct control.
treatment_switch: VLLM_ASCEND_HYPIC_ENABLE=0 versus 1; evidence-file path is arm-specific

time_budget.launch_order: baseline terminal and independently audited before candidate
time_budget.timeout_rule: An observation timeout is ambiguous; inspect the same controller and exact owned resources, never launch a duplicate.

primary_observations: per-sample correctness and finish reason in all three scored repetitions
identical response prefix length across arms and within arm
per-request four-worker hot proof joined to scored request ID
continuous physical NPU0-3 isolation and exact owned release
decision_rule: Diagnostic only. If candidate differs with clean serial isolation and proved hot activation, c32 contention is not necessary for that observed difference. If serial outputs converge, c32 cache/scheduling remains a hypothesis. Incomplete/variable results are inconclusive. No three-sample outcome may overturn r19 or establish population quality preservation.
admission: Before each arm: fresh direct chicaihong01/ma route, loaded host-development contract, physical NPU0-3 and port 8223 actually idle, exact new root absent, source/model hashes valid, prior arm terminal and released. Never touch foreign tasks or NPU4-7.
